# Texture Packing and Atlas Organization


## Overview
Texture Packing and Atlas Organization consolidates multiple volumetric data sources or semantic channels into fewer, larger texture resources to optimize memory bandwidth, reduce state changes, and emulate 3D texture support in constrained environments [G]. It differs from [3D Texture Storage and Sampling](3064-3d-texture-storage-and-sampling.md) by focusing on the logical arrangement of data within the resource rather than the hardware storage format, and from [Sparse Volume Texture (SVT)](7011-sparse-volume-texture-svt.md) by keeping data dense and resident rather than sparse and paged [G].

## Shared principles
The family shares the goal of reducing the number of active texture units and state transitions by grouping data [G]. The core mechanism involves mapping logical data indices (whether semantic channels, discrete volumes, or spatial slices) into a single physical texture coordinate space [G]. This requires a deterministic mapping function in the shader to reconstruct the logical coordinate from the physical one [G]. The method assumes the target hardware supports the resulting texture format (e.g., 3D textures, 2D arrays, or multi-channel 2D textures) [G].

## Subtopics

### [Texture Uniting (Multi-Channel Packing)](2470-texture-uniting-multi-channel-packing.md)
Combines multiple separate 3D textures into a single RGBA 3D texture to optimize memory bandwidth and sampling efficiency [G]. Unlike [3D Volume Atlas Packing](7158-3d-volume-atlas-packing.md), it packs semantic attributes into color channels of a single volume, allowing simultaneous access to all attributes at a single coordinate. Choose when rendering volumes with multiple attribute channels that must be sampled together.

### [3D Volume Atlas Packing](7158-3d-volume-atlas-packing.md)
Consolidates multiple discrete 3D volumes into a single physical 3D texture resource, reducing the number of active texture units and state transitions [G]. It differs from [Texture Uniting (Multi-Channel Packing)](2470-texture-uniting-multi-channel-packing.md) by handling distinct volumetric datasets along a dedicated atlas dimension. Choose when managing multiple distinct volumetric datasets, such as animation timesteps.

### [Image Texture Atlas Packing](11896-image-texture-atlas-packing.md)
Represents 3D volumetric data as a set of 2D image slices arranged into a single 2D texture atlas [G]. It differs from [3D Volume Atlas Packing](7158-3d-volume-atlas-packing.md) by explicitly targeting the constraints of legacy web graphics APIs (e.g., WebGL 1.0) using a matrix-based 2D layout, and from [Texture Uniting (Multi-Channel Packing)](2470-texture-uniting-multi-channel-packing.md) by organizing spatial slices rather than semantic channels. Choose for compatibility with environments lacking native 3D texture support.

### [Per-tile empty-space skip with contrast-normalized min/max metadata](12685-per-tile-empty-space-skip-with-contrast-normalized-min-max-m.md)
A rendering-side optimization that skips raymarch stepping through resident-but-empty tiles by comparing tile-local density bounds against a global contrast floor [G]. It differs from its siblings, which focus on memory packing, by operating on the raymarching logic itself, using metadata to avoid unnecessary sampling and shading calculations. Choose to bypass empty regions within already-loaded data.
